raw_segments.text: Having arranged matters thus, Denísov and Dólokhov intended, without reporting matters
to the higher command, to attack and seize that convoy with their own small forces.
On October 22nd it was moving from the village of Mikúlino to that of Shámshevo.
To the left of the road between Mikúlino and Shámshevo there were large forests,
extending in some places up to the road itself though in others a mile or more back from it.
Through these forests Denísov and his party rode all day,
sometimes keeping well back in them and sometimes coming to the very edge,
but never losing sight of the moving French. That morning, carsacks of Denísov's party
had seized and carried off into the forest two wagons loaded with cavalry saddles,
which had stuck in the mud not far from Mikúlino where the forest ran close to the road.
Since then, and until evening, the party had watched the movement of the French without
attacking. It was necessary to let the French reach Shámshevo quietly without alarming them
and then, after joining Dólokhov who was to come that evening to a consultation at a watchman's hut
in the forest less than a mile from Shámshevo, to surprise the French at dawn, falling like an
avalanche on their heads from two sides, and rout and capture them all at one blow.
